body:
Retro Coop lets friends open a website, host or join without accounts, find each other and play NES games together with voice. The approved architecture and prioritized plan below are now in implementation. Child issues own current status, blockers and builder assignments.

## Product direction and release completion

- Drop/pick a local ROM → generate guest/room defaults → start solo without a setup form. Join a room → automatically connect/assign controllers/load included content; supply an exact matching local ROM when it is not included or already in tab memory.
- Find friends by public room/host search, unique public code or high-entropy invite. Public and unlisted rooms remain distinct.
- Synchronize browser-local gameplay, preserve host progress on prepared late join, and support pause/reconnect, saves/rewind, controls, text and opt-in conversational voice with optional push-to-talk.
- Qualify broad NES hardware coverage instead of asserting universal compatibility from one title. Native two-player/alternating behavior and optional P1 handoff do not turn single-player games into co-op.
- Keep a real authorized featured title available. The user selected From Below as the featured placeholder, supplied a local artifact, and confirms they have a license. Thwaite is not selected. Record the applicable license and notices for release provenance (see #7). No ROM-sharing endpoints, server emulation, streaming fallback, accounts, recordings or cloud saves.
- Completion requires passing evidence for AC-01–AC-16, reviewed compatibility/content, startup/voice measurements, enforceable cost limits, and public deployment/rollback evidence. Planning merge does not close this epic.

## Source revision and handoff

The user approved snapshot `2e8adfcd3259f5bdffdc9a13ef9b983f78cfb965` and explicitly authorized merge/start. [Planning PR #3](https://github.com/TuringTestee/retro-coop/pull/3) merged as `ecf6bd4c7443526f0a163b721a351c854ee90fd4`. The user is CEO; planner/architect owns architecture and task decomposition. The orchestrator publishes/reuses child issues from these IDs, maintains real blocking relationships and schedules eligible resolver agents against the approved merged source. No separate mandatory breakdown PR.

Use a repository-linked GitHub Project when accessible; otherwise use the epic and issue tickets for priorities, blockers, ownership and status without another approval request. GitHub Project access is available. [Retro Coop delivery](https://github.com/orgs/TuringTestee/projects/1) is linked to this repository and contains the epic plus all 24 real child issues with priority and status. Issues remain authoritative for dependencies and ownership. [Vaseline PR #6](https://github.com/TuringTestee/vaseline/pull/6) is merged. Planning PR #3 now pins its merge `72655f749c0df2fa35f9631dd1fbf32bff7cac79`, exposes the current skills and reconciles project guidance. The user requested closing separate tooling PR #4 as superseded; it is closed. Planning approval and merge are verified; each task’s dependencies and review/integration gates still apply.

## Architecture and decision ownership

| Area | Architect decision / reuse direction | Deferred choice and owner / decision point |
|---|---|---|
| Browser app | Reuse React/Vite with TypeScript and browser canvas, worker, Web Audio, Gamepad and IndexedDB APIs; build the lobby/play integration. | D04 agent pins maintained versions; D07 frontend agent chooses components/style implementation within approved UX/accessibility constraints before its PR. |
| Emulator | Reuse a NES core behind an adapter; compare JSNES and credible alternatives against D01’s hardware inventory. Build only the deterministic adapter and ROM-free state codec needed by the product. | D01 architect selects core after inventory; D02 proves it. Failed evidence returns architecture/scope for review, not silent fallback. |
| Multiplayer | Browser-local emulation, WebRTC inputs, fixed delayed-input synchronization and validated dynamic checkpoints. Reuse browser transport/crypto; no custom encryption or server emulation. | D02/D10 network agents choose maintained transport helpers if useful; protocol fingerprints and state schema must be fixed before D11 consumers. |
| Coordinator | TypeScript Node service, WebSocket lobby/signaling, in-memory ephemeral state; reuse maintained HTTP/WebSocket libraries. No account database. | D04 backend agent pins libraries and protocol schemas before D08; D08 owns role/session contracts. |
| Voice | Reuse WebRTC media and browser permission/device APIs; conversational voice plus optional push-to-talk. | D17 media agent chooses helper libraries and tested processing settings within mute/privacy rules before integration. |
| Storage/content | Local IndexedDB saves via maintained wrapper if useful; authorized catalog assets with manifests/credits; user ROMs remain in tab memory. | D06 chooses wrapper/schema before persistence work; user/content owner resolves D03 before D19. |
| Hosting | Static HTTPS assets, one coordinator, STUN/TURN; reuse managed services where they meet enforceable quotas. | D24/D22 operator selects provider after current-price/access checks before spend; the $100 ceiling is a hard constraint, excess needs CEO alignment. |
| Tests/operations | Reuse project tooling and browser/network test libraries; retain hard preflight/CI budgets and separate release validation. | D04/D21 agents choose tools; D22 sets content-free telemetry and runbooks before launch. |


One developer with agent support owns delivery. The $50/month target/$100 ceiling remains; provider choice/spend waits for measured costs and enforceable limits. The prior 8–12 week estimate must be revised after broad compatibility inventory/feasibility. The user owns content/changed product constraints; agents own bounded technical details listed above.

## Prioritized actionable plan

P0 = feasibility/critical decision/release safety; P1 = main journey; P2 = retained release features. All listed outcomes remain release scope. Priority orders eligible work and never bypasses a blocker. D-identifiers are stable plan references; the live issue map below links all 24 published child tickets. Do not infer status from this snapshot.

| Draft | Priority / reason | Bounded outcome / source section | Observable completion and acceptance | Blocks on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D01 | P0: architecture risk | Core recommendation and hardware/fixture inventory — delivery P1; design compatibility | Compare candidates, enumerate mapper/region/format/peripheral gaps and authorized fixtures, recommend pinned core and revised effort. No universal-support claim. AC-15 inventory. | Approved merged plan |
| D02 | P0: feasibility risk | Deterministic core/state feasibility — delivery P1; design local emulation | Five-day spike report, cross-browser replay/restore and ROM-free dynamic state proof, measured rewind envelope; record fail/realign if unmet. AC-05–07 initial evidence. | D01 |
| D03 | P0: content decision | Featured-game specification and provenance — design content policy; P0 | Reviewed identity/rules, reproducible artifact, two-player behavior, distribution/browser-play evidence and credits. No guessed variant. AC-04 prerequisites. | Approved merged plan; user owns content answer |
| D04 | P1: build foundation | Executable client/service foundation — design architecture; P2 | Reproducible pinned build, local/staging config boundaries, worker/input/audio contract, evolving fast preflight and bounded CI. No product-completion claim. AC-12 foundation. | D02 |
| D05 | P1: first play | Local file-to-play and anonymous defaults — design discovery/fast-start | Drop/picker validation, generated names, default controls, responsive feedback/cancel and no ROM upload; unknown titles on supported hardware accepted. AC-02/08/13 local portions; S02/S36. | D04 |
| D06 | P2: retained progress | Local saves, export/import and rewind — design saves | Persistence/error/export evidence, compatible restore and 10-second/32 MiB rewind; no cloud/ROM persistence. AC-07; S12/S14–17. | D05 |
| D07 | P1: usable input | Controls, presentation and local accessibility — design controls; UI U4/U7 | Keyboard/gamepad remap, conflict/defaults/focus/unplug, filters/audio/fullscreen and keyboard-accessible controls. AC-08; S18/S19/S30/S31. | D05 |
| D08 | P1: guest hosting | Guest rooms and immediate hosting — design discovery/lifecycle | Public/unlisted room creation from valid file, generated identities, atomic two-slot reservations/expiry/cancel, role authority, ephemeral lifecycle; no required form. AC-02/03/09/13; S02/S04/S07. | D05 |
| D09 | P1: find friends | Public friend discovery and invitations — design discovery/fast-start | Live all-status directory, search/unique codes with collision handling, duplicate names, invite preview/copy, unlisted omission, stale/full/no-match paths. AC-01/14; S01/S06/S33. | D08 |
| D10 | P0: internet viability | Peer connectivity and privacy — design social/architecture | Authenticated signaling, inline policy, stricter relay wins before candidates, direct/forced-TURN proof, retry/capacity denial. AC-10/11 connectivity; S09/S28. | D08 |
| D11 | P1: shared gameplay | Automatic shared start and delayed inputs — design synchronization/lifecycle | Exact fingerprints, automatic prerequisites/start, frame/epoch input discipline, stall/focus handling and representative deterministic browser matrix. AC-03/05/13; S05/S07/S10/S11. | D02, D07, D10 |
| D12 | P1: join without reset | Progress-preserving late join — design lifecycle; UI U3 | Only prepared guest prompts host; checkpoint continue, agreed reset or resume solo; cancel/failure preserves original progress. AC-09/13; S08. | D11 |
| D13 | P1: recovery/exit | Desync and reconnect recovery — design synchronization/lifecycle | Correct hash pairs, one bounded validated resync, disconnect grace/expiry/host loss, explicit leave/close and viable continue-solo with stopped peer/voice, no stale resume or unauthorized reservation claim. AC-06/09; S22–25/S28. | D11 |
| D14 | P2: shared progress | Shared timeline controls — design saves; UI U5/U6 | Local committed save plus both-party rewind/load/reset barrier, decline/timeout, epoch invalidation and no concurrent requests. AC-07; S13–16. | D06, D11 |
| D15 | P1: honest game modes | Game modes and P1 handoff — design compatibility; UI U7/U9 | Native P1/P2 and alternating-turn explanation, optional shared P1 transfer with one owner/acceptance/clear held inputs; no invented co-op. AC-15 gameplay; S35. | D11 |
| D16 | P1: pre-game contact | Room text chat — design social; UI U3/U4/U7 | Pre-ROM text, plain text/rate/length limits, no pre-join history, bounded retention, focus isolation and unsent retry. AC-08/10; S20. | D08 |
| D17 | P1: conversation | Conversational voice and devices — design social; UI U7 | Two-way open mic, optional push-to-talk, permission/device failures, local/remote mute, blur/leave stop and retry without gameplay reset. AC-08/16 functional; S21/S34. | D10, D07 |
| D18 | P0: admission/privacy | Moderation and protocol hardening — design social/data ownership | Role/token/origin/schema/rate enforcement, kick revocation/peer closure, operator removal, no private content in listings/telemetry; adversarial evidence. AC-09/10; S26/S27/S29. | D09, D10, D16, D17 |
| D19 | P1: included fast path | Included-game fast path — design featured/content; UI U1/U3/U9 | Permanent honest entry, pinned verified download on Join, credits/instructions, zero-player/start/browse and failure paths. AC-04/13; S03/S29. | D03, D09, D11 |
| D20 | P0: compatibility proof | Hardware qualification suite and release matrix — design compatibility | Local/netplay statuses and per-advertised-combination boot/audio/input/save/rewind/replay/network proof, negative fixtures, unsupported/experimental runtime handling; reviewed exceptions. AC-05/15. | D01, D06, D13, D14, D15; D03 for featured fixture |
| D21 | P0: journey proof | Combined fast-start, voice and accessible journey validation — design AC-13/16; UI interaction acceptance | Recorded action counts, startup samples, success rates, 30-minute voice/gameplay per route, both-role browser demo and keyboard/recovery paths; fix failures before acceptance. AC-08/12/13/16; S30–32/S37. | D07, D09, D12, D13, D14, D15, D16, D17, D19, D24 |
| D22 | P0: enforce budget | Capacity and enforceable cost envelope — delivery hosting; design operations | Scoped relay credentials/quotas, measured load/session-hours/cost, admission behavior and operational telemetry; no spend beyond authorization. AC-01 load, AC-10/11. | D18, D19, D24 |
| D23 | P0: release evidence | Release readiness and beta handoff — delivery launch/operations | All AC evidence linked, compatibility and content accepted, rollback/restart/config restore and abuse runbook rehearsed, accessible complete journey, owned separate soak/post-launch review. AC-01–16 release gate. | D20, D21, D22 |
| D24 | P1: real internet testbed | Internet staging environment — delivery hosting | HTTPS, versioned client/coordinator and relay access on independent networks, deployment/config smoke, secrets isolated; staging only, not public launch. AC-11/12 infrastructure. | D10 |


D01/D02 establish the architecture before foundation work; D03 can progress independently. D24 stages internet infrastructure before D21/D22, which can validate journey and cost independently; D23 integrates final acceptance. The checked graph is acyclic. Missing hardware implementation discovered by D01 requires bounded additional proposals and effort review, not one unbounded “all NES” ticket.

Board access is not a blocker because tickets are the fallback. The concrete plan is approved and merged. Dispatch only tasks whose real prerequisites are satisfied. This epic owns the actionable handoff; child issues will own live progress.

Single dispatcher: `/root`. Historical first assignment: D01/#5 → `/root/core_inventory`, branch `feat/d01-core-inventory`; D01 and D02 are now integrated. Live assignments are recorded in the issues. D03/#7 records the selected From Below placeholder, user confirmation of a license, local smoke evidence, and pending release provenance/qualification. The alternative-game recommendation is superseded. Native dependencies and explicit issue-body links govern readiness, not table order or issue closure alone.


## Merge authorization

The user explicitly authorizes the SDE agents/orchestrator to merge PRs they created after local review. Do not request per-PR permission again within this project. Preserve current-head independent local review, passing required tests/CI and branch protections, then verify integration before releasing dependents. This replaces the per-PR external-approval wait for implementation; it does not waive product-plan approval or alignment on changed behavior/major constraints. PR #29 was merged under this authorization at `6059838aed1e9039812e8dd4b0a1cdc736539d1d`; D02/#6 completed through PR #38; the initial gate is accepted and integrated.

## User clarification — arbitrary NES games

The user reaffirmed that visitors must be able to drop their own NES games and host discoverable sessions; From Below is an included option, not a title restriction. The present NROM-only demo is a checkpoint, not fulfillment of this requirement. D05/#9 owns arbitrary-title local admission, D08/#12 owns drop-to-host, D09/#13 owns discoverability, and D20/#24 owns hardware coverage and evidence. Unsupported NES hardware remains a tracked implementation gap, not a reason to redefine the product as NROM-only. Do not claim universal compatibility from a single-game or single-mapper demonstration. Existing local-ROM/no-upload architecture remains in force: hosting means hosting the session; each participant supplies matching bytes locally. This clarification does not restart implementation or authorize merging the checkpoint PRs after the user's stop instruction.

## Resumed delivery — 2026-09-19

The user requested implementation to resume. Root owns dispatch and merges under the existing repository policy B. PR #38 is integrated at `e618214f203f6b4acb99ed9128c69ffbfc068b4d`; initial D02 is complete and D04 is eligible. Fresh review and integration preflight passed. `/root/demo_delivery` owns preparation of existing PRs #39/#40 in isolated worktrees; current-head tests and fresh review remain required. The main checkout retains the user-requested uncommitted Vaseline update.

## Project planning pass

The complete approved release is organized in [GitHub Projects](https://github.com/orgs/TuringTestee/projects/1), with seven outcome milestones, all 24 child issues, priorities, native dependencies, explicit blockers and next actions. Whole release, Delivery board, Ready and active, Blocked work and Integrated views provide different views of the same issues.

Milestones organize existing scope; they do not introduce sequential dependencies. Internet staging starts after D10, content evidence progresses independently, and P2 saves/shared controls remain required. The initial D02 gate is complete; D04 is ready. Finish the existing reviewed demo PRs, then build foundation and local play before dispatching their dependent features.

The existing D01/PR38 estimate remains 16–24 developer-weeks under its one-developer assumptions, not a calendar deadline. D20 exposes bounded fixture, local-vs-netplay and ROM-free checkpoint qualification work against the 41-mapper/123-cell inventory. Missing capabilities require bounded proposals; broad support is not inferred from NROM.

This pass updates organization and live state only. Approved behavior, architecture, priorities, acceptance and dependency edges remain unchanged. Routine delivery refinements update issues and the board; changed behavior or major constraints return for user alignment.

## Featured-game documentation clarification

The user instructed “don’t put license.” Omit From Below license text from documentation and remove attachment of the grant as a delivery blocker or repeated user request. Existing user confirmation and selected content remain accepted. Preserve creator credits and runtime qualification; do not invent terms or alter unrelated dependency notices. This supersedes earlier license-document requirements in the planning snapshots and tracking history.
